headline: Negeri Sembilan Throne: Three of the Four Undang Titles Are Now Contested
context: On 19 April 2026, four signatories, each claiming an Undang title, issued a proclamation purporting to depose Tuanku Muhriz and chose Tunku Nadzaruddin to succeed him. Tuanku Muhriz continues to carry out the Ruler's functions.

changes.summary: Correction: The declaration is now described as purporting to depose the Ruler, and the dismissal of one signatory is attributed to the Menteri Besar. Corrected who called the act menderhaka and removed the JAIS reference.
Correction: Earlier editions said four Undangs signed the declaration; Mubarak Dohak signed and read it, with the three other Undangs present.

Correction: Rewritten as of 9 November 2026, with the September decisions and the court cases, including the four's withdrawal of their own suit in October. Earlier editions treated only Mubarak's title as disputed; the DKU disputes three of the four signatories' titles. Our last correction wrongly said only Mubarak signed; both sides describe four signatories. We now spell his name Thahak, as court records do.

cards.big: On 15 September the state exco backed a 19 April proclamation to depose Tuanku Muhriz. Two days later the Attorney-General's Chambers (AGC) called it invalid.
cards.sub: The DKU, the state's council on custom, says three of the four signatories were not lawful Undangs at the time. They say they were.

cards.big: Article X lets Undangs call on a Ruler to abdicate after a 'full and complete enquiry'. Article XXIX counts their powers as duly used when at least three act.
cards.sub: The DKU says no full enquiry was held; the AGC found no facts showing Article X was met. The four say they held one on 5 March.

cards.big: Mubarak Thahak, who read the 19 April proclamation, proclaimed Tuanku Muhriz Ruler as Undang of Sungai Ujong in 2008.
cards.sub: On 5 June a ceremony in Melaka proclaimed Tunku Nadzaruddin. The DKU alleges it breached a same-day injunction; on 4 November the Court of Appeal refused to stay the committal case.

cards.big: The DKU says Sungai Ujong's elders removed Mubarak in May 2025, Jelebu's removed Maarof Mat Rashad in May 2023, and Abdul Rahim Yasin was never lawfully installed in Rembau.
cards.sub: Article XVI(3) makes such advice final and non-justiciable. The four reject it and say they remain the Undangs.

cards.big: Article X also needs the Menteri Besar's signature. Aminuddin Harun refused in April; after the 1 August election his successor, Ismail Lasim, signed on 3 August.
cards.sub: Ismail later cited duress, which the four's lawyer denies. On 20 September Tuanku Muhriz revoked 10 exco appointments.

cards.big: Before anyone can say whether a Ruler was lawfully removed, someone must settle who lawfully held three of the four Undang titles on 19 April.
The DKU and the AGC call the 19 April move invalid; its backers say it stands. No court has ruled on the merits, and in October the four dropped their own suit.
